issues: The character label “The king of the Lamanites” is supported, but the king’s depicted appearance and surroundings remain unspecified.
The people and specific moment depicted are unspecified; keep the image to the stated action of laying weapons down, without implying a battle or identifying individuals.
The listed communities are not established as gathered at one time or place; portray them separately if visualized together.
“They hardened their own hearts” adds “own”; verse 14 says they hardened their hearts and the hearts of the Lamanites.

The narration excerpt from verse 15 is a contiguous quotation, but ends before the verse specifies that the cities were those in which people repented, came to know the truth, and were converted. This omission is not an ellipsis, but the excerpt alone is incomplete.

The visual contrast is a permissible inference only if it does not imply the groups shared a time or place; the previous scene explicitly warns that the converted communities are not one simultaneous gathering.
The consultation is explicit, but its setting, participants’ appearance, and words exchanged are unspecified; do not invent dialogue.
The nature of the industrious work and the form of correspondence are unspecified; the verses do not establish Nephites physically present.
